description: Single-panel polythermal (isoplethal) section of a Fe-Mn-Al-C phase diagram, labelled (b) in Fig. 10, calculated with FactSage for C = 0.85% and Al = 7%. Temperature T (°C) is on the y-axis (200-1600 °C, ticks every 200 °C) and Mn content Mn (wt%) on the x-axis (0-30, ticks every 5); the left origin is marked "Fe". Solid curves bound the labelled phase fields: L (liquid) at the top above ~1400 °C, then L+δ, γ+δ at the right, a large central γ (austenite) field, γ+α at upper left, α+κ at lower left, α+γ+κ, α+κ+M23C6, B2+κ and B2+κ+M7C3 near the bottom left, γ+κ and γ+κ+B2 at mid-right, and γ+κ+M23C6+B2, B2+κ+M23C6 and B2+β+M23C6+κ at bottom right. An almost horizontal boundary near 760 °C bounds the γ+κ field. A dashed line runs from ~1000 °C at 0 wt% Mn, falling to ~900 °C around 10 wt% Mn and continuing into the lower-right corner near 380 °C; dash-dotted curves bound the κ-carbide formation region. Per the caption the dashed lines are the disorder-to-order transition temperature and the dash-dotted lines the κ-phase formation temperature. The figure demonstrates the equilibrium phase sequence of an Fe-Mn-Al-0.85C alloy with 7 wt% Al as Mn is varied from 0 to 30 wt%.

subfigures.description: Polythermal phase-diagram section of Fe-Mn-Al-0.85C at Al = 7%, plotted as T (°C) from 200 to 1600 versus Mn (wt%) from 0 to 30 (origin marked 'Fe'). Solid boundaries define L, L+δ, γ+δ, γ, γ+α, γ+κ, α+κ, α+γ+κ, α+κ+M23C6, B2+κ, B2+κ+M7C3, γ+κ+B2, γ+κ+M23C6+B2, B2+κ+M23C6 and B2+β+M23C6+κ fields; dashed and dash-dotted lines mark disorder-to-order and κ-formation temperatures.

observations.observation: The plotted axes are Mn (wt%) on the x-axis (0-30, tick spacing 5) and T (°C) on the y-axis (200-1600, tick spacing 200), with the left intercept labelled 'Fe'.
A large central phase field is labelled γ (austenite), extending from roughly 900 °C down to about 500 °C across the whole 0-30 wt% Mn range.
The upper region contains L (liquid) above ~1400 °C and a band labelled L+δ beneath it, with a γ+δ field on the right-hand side.
Lower-left fields are labelled α+κ, B2+κ and B2+κ+M7C3, while the bottom-right corner contains γ+κ+B2, γ+κ+M23C6+B2, B2+κ+M23C6 and B2+β+M23C6+κ.
An almost horizontal boundary near 760 °C separates γ from the γ+κ field on the right of the diagram.
The figure shows dashed and dash-dotted lines in addition to solid phase boundaries, indicating transition temperatures overlaid on the equilibrium fields.
The caption states the dash-dotted lines are the formation temperature of the κ phase and the dashed lines are the disorder-to-order transition temperature.
The caption states panel (b) is the polythermal section as a function of Mn for Al = 7% and C = 0.85% (i.e. the Mn-axis section shown here).
The caption states the polythermal sections of the Fe-Mn-Al-0.85C phase diagrams were calculated from FactSage.
The citing text states Fig. 10 shows phase diagrams of Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys as a function of Mn for a fixed C content of 0.85% and Al content of 7%.
The phase fields include the ordered B2 phase and M23C6 and M7C3 carbides at low temperature, showing that ordering and carbide precipitation compete with the austenite field as Mn increases.

unreadable_items: The exact wording near the two closely spaced α+κ+M23C6 labels around 8-12 wt% Mn is crowded and partially overlapping
The dash-dotted κ-formation lines are not individually labelled inside the plot, so which curves are dash-dotted versus dashed is difficult to distinguish in the lower-right corner
